strings.name: Yao Ming
strings.summary: Yao Ming led Shanghai to a CBA title before joining the Houston Rockets as the NBA’s first draft pick. An eight-time All-Star, he became an important link between Chinese and international basketball. Injuries ended his playing career in 2011. He then pursued philanthropy and governance, chairing the Chinese Basketball Association from 2017 to 2024. He continued youth-sports work afterward, attending a Hong Kong charity class in November 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Hall of Fame recognition and basketball governance connected Chinese and international basketball markets.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting basketball cultures
strings.highlights.h1.text: Eight NBA playing seasons and eight All-Star selections, alongside national-team service, linked different basketball audiences and cultures.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Developed in Shanghai’s youth system; studied at Shanghai Jiao Tong University after retirement and completed an economics degree in 2018.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Philanthropy and governance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Founded the Yao Foundation and promoted youth sport; his association tenure combined reforms with pressure from the men’s team’s repeated Olympic qualification failures.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Hong Kong charity class
strings.timeline.t1.text: Joined Li Xiaopeng and Deng Yaping at a youth touch-rugby activity, discussing sport’s contribution to psychological resilience.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Left the association presidency
strings.timeline.t2.text: His resignation was approved and Guo Zhenming succeeded him; he no longer chaired the association.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Elected association president
strings.timeline.t3.text: Began leading the Chinese Basketball Association, working on league, youth and sport-education reforms; re-elected in 2022.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Basketball Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.t4.text: Entered the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in recognition of his playing career and international influence.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Injury-enforced retirement
strings.timeline.t5.text: Retired after repeated foot injuries, turning to philanthropy, study and basketball administration.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Established the Yao Foundation
strings.timeline.t6.text: Launched philanthropy after the Sichuan earthquake, developing a platform supporting education and rural youth basketball.
strings.timeline.t7.title: CBA title and NBA entry
strings.timeline.t7.text: Led Shanghai to the CBA championship and became the NBA’s first overall pick, joining Houston that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Professional start in Shanghai
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined the Shanghai Sharks’ senior team and developed into a leading domestic centre.
